q-130096.prompt_mask: Given the function $f(x,y)=@@F@@,$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=@@P@@.$
q-130096.solution_mask:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=@@P@@:$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(@@F@@)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(@@F@@)\,j \\  & =@@DX@@\,i+@@DY@@\,j \\ ∇f@@P@@ & =@@EX@@\,i+@@EY@@\,j \\  & =@@BASIS@@ \\  & =@@GRAD@@\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f@@P@@\cdot @@DISP_RAW@@ & =0 \\ @@GRAD@@\cdot @@DISP@@ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
